name: dTRINITY Staked dUSD
oneLiner: sdUSD is dTRINITY's yield-bearing dUSD vault receipt; staked dUSD is supplied into dLEND and the share price accrues lending yield.
collateral: dUSD deposited into dTRINITY dSTAKE vaults and supplied into dLEND; deployments are chain-isolated and non-fungible across networks.
pegMechanism: Stake dUSD to mint sdUSD vault receipts and unstake back into dUSD when dLEND liquidity is available; dSTAKE charges no staking fee, unstaking can incur up to 10 bps retained by the vault, and NAV appreciates as dLEND supply APY accrues.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: READY_FOR_REPLAY: official documentation lists only the Ethereum and Fraxtal sdUSD vault receipts and states that deployments are chain-isolated. At Ethereum block 25535363, proxy 0x7cb20517776636ed76b68edb3d99dcce356abf02 resolved through its EIP-1967 implementation slot to DStakeTokenV2 0x9c278036c3c4529472751502dfc71bb1f0a3bfd4; ProxyAdmin 0xbe90db309b80357631069b689fc3481aca2c65be was owned by TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b, which held the token DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and had a 86400-second delay. The live router was 0xdd26c236ec95d03ddf3cb67b7f54864719e9be5a, paused() was false, and current normal ERC20/ERC4626 withdrawals and public solver paths honor allowance whenever caller differs from owner. Router PAUSER_ROLE can pause deposits and redemptions, not token transfers. However, this is not inherited-only: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can call migrateCore() after the timelock, and its only candidate checks are the reported dStakeToken and collateralVault. A candidate router satisfying those checks can call router-only burnFromRouter() with initiator equal to owner, reaching its allowance-bypass branch and burning that holder's shares. This source-derived mutable holder-seizure route is direct possible, not an active blacklist/true finding. At Fraxtal block 38637738, proxy 0x58acc2600835211dcb5847c5fa422791fd492409 resolved to exact-match DStakeToken 0x0f51b15939a42bd995ecd3a2c151dc58621856c6; its DStakeProxyAdmin 0xde914ec384346fea47339e5086d2d399b7f4733b was owned by 0x0bafaDA2a5824864720873EE40cd960b36445212. The current Fraxtal implementation has ordinary ERC20/ERC4626 allowance behavior and no live blacklist/pause/transfer-hook/arbitrary-holder-burn function, but its upgrade owner can change that code. The separately documented dUSD/dTRINITY upstream exposure remains additional; this direct possible review does not suppress it. The Terms describe interface/protocol restrictions and upgrades in general terms but do not establish a current token-holder blacklist. Archive.org returned no snapshot for the reviewed sdUSD docs or Terms URL.

notices.title: Liquidity-gated unstaking
notices.message: sdUSD unstaking depends on available dUSD liquidity in dLEND; when utilization is high, holders may need to wait for borrowers to repay or sell sdUSD on secondary markets.

mintAuthority.summary: sdUSD (dSTAKE vault) is upgradeable via ProxyAdmin owned by a 24-hour TimelockController, whose proposer/executor/canceller is a single 3-of-5 Safe multisig (0xe83c188...). Shares are minted only by staking dUSD — no privileged mint surface. Fraxtal has a distinct proxy-admin path whose terminal signer policy is unverified.

controls.label: dSTAKE Ethereum upgrade Safe (via 24-hour TimelockController)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295192, the sdUSD proxy admin was ProxyAdmin 0xbe90db309b80357631069b689fc3481aca2c65be, whose owner is TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b with minDelay 86400 seconds. That timelock's proposer, canceller, and executor roles resolve to this Safe. At block 25573508 the Safe returned the five owners recorded here, threshold 3, and no enabled modules; the current upgrade path can change wrapper mint logic after the delay.

controls.label: dSTAKE sdUSD vault share accounting (Ethereum)
controls.capDescription: Ethereum sdUSD shares are minted only against deposited local dUSD and do not create base dUSD supply.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25570988, asset() on the dSTAKE vault returned local dUSD 0x07fff99e1664d9b116fbc158c0e99785f81ca236. The current vault share path is deposit-backed accounting.

controls.label: Inherited dUSD AMO/governed-reserve mint authority
controls.evidence: Underlying dUSD is minted 1:1 against a governance-set whitelist of reserve stablecoins, with AMO pre-minting dUSD into Curve pools and contributor governance (pre-TGE multisig) controlling the whitelist, AMO/SMO, and a mint kill-switch. sdUSD inherits this concentrated-admin posture, plus the March 17 2026 dTRINITY exploit exposure noted on the dUSD profile.

review.evidence: Ethereum control review is current: ProxyAdmin 0xbe90db309b80357631069b689fc3481aca2c65be is owned by the 86400-second TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b, which resolves to the reviewed 3-of-5 Safe. The local wrapper share path is dUSD-deposit backed. Fraxtal has a distinct transparent proxy and DStakeProxyAdmin 0xde914ec384346fea47339e5086d2d399b7f4733b, whose owner is an EOA; its terminal signer policy and any delay are not established by the reviewed sources.
unresolvedQuestions: Verify the terminal owner, signer policy, delay, and upgrade permissions of the Fraxtal DStakeProxyAdmin 0xde914ec384346fea47339e5086d2d399b7f4733b before treating the two-deployment sdUSD mint and code-change authority as complete.
